Coefficient Estimation via Julia

Source: R/BetaEstimate.R
Beta_estimate.Rd

Calls the Julia function Beta_estimate to obtain coefficient estimates for OLS, GLM, multivariate-normal, or multinomial models. When family = "auto" Julia chooses the estimator automatically.

Usage

Beta_estimate(
  X,
  Y,
  family = "auto",
  link = "auto",
  n_trials = NULL,
  theta = NULL,
  add_intercept = TRUE
)

Arguments

X

Numeric design matrix (\(n \times p\)).

Y

Numeric vector (\(n\)) or matrix (\(n \times q\)) of responses. A one-column matrix is automatically converted to a vector.

family

One of "auto" (default, guessed from Y), "Linear" (or "Normal"), "MultivariateNormal", "Bernoulli", "Binomial", "Poisson", "Gamma", "Exponential", "InverseGaussian", "NegativeBinomial", "Geometric", or "Multinomial" (one-vs-rest logistic). The default links match LP_to_Y(): identity, logit, or log.

link

Character/symbol/Julia Link; default "auto".

n_trials

Integer trials for a binomial response (default NULL).

theta

Optional NegativeBinomial size; estimated from the data if NULL.

add_intercept

Logical. If TRUE (default) the wrapper asks Julia to prepend a column of 1s and keeps the intercept coefficient in the returned vector/matrix. Set to FALSE if X already contains an intercept column.

Value

Numeric vector or matrix of coefficients (intercept first if add_intercept = TRUE).
